opener.dateline:
Ministry of Foreign Affairs,
Cairo, June 18, 1880.

div.p: Sir: Upon the occasion of the promulgation of the decree of His Highness the Khedive relating to the institution of the commission of liquidation, the representatives of Germany, Austria-Hungary, France, Great Britain, and Italy, signed, upon the 31st day of March last, a declaration by which their governments bind themselves to accept as obligatory and without appeal the decisions that shall be rendered by this commission so far as the obligations and debts of the Egyptian Government and of the Daïra, Sanieh, and Khassa are concerned.

The adhesion of the Government of the United States and of the other powers that have taken part in the judicial reform being necessary in order that the decisions of the commission he recognized by the mixed tribunals as an obligatory law so soon as they (i. e. the decisions) shall have been officially published by the government of His Highness the Khedive, I now solicit, through your kindness, the support of the Government of the United States in favor of the declaration in question, being convinced that the Washington cabinet will recognize the advantages that will be afforded to all parties interested by the settlement of the Egyptian debt brought about through a common agreement.

The delay that would be naturally occasioned by asking for this adhesion by letter, leads me, Mr. Agent and Consul-General, in view more especially of the near termination
of the labors of the commission, to appeal to your wonted courtesy and ask you to kindly transmit by telegraph the request that I have the honor to address to you in the name of the Government of His Highness, and beg you to solicit of the cabinet of Washington a reply by telegraph also.

closer.signed:
MUSTAPHA FEHMI,
Minister of Foreign Affairs.

postscript.p:
E. E. Farman, Esq.,
Agent and Consul-General of the United States.
